title: zazzle invoker component diagram
description: The invoker's source, its tests and its benchmarks, the daemon all three need, and the standalone tools the invoker runs for `zazzle free-disk-space` and `zazzle fix-network`. The same program, run as `zazz` or under an installed script's name, sends zazz requests to the daemon.

components.name: zazzle invoker
components.responsibility: Builds and tests the zazzle program.

components.name: Invoker source
components.responsibility: The program: logic, entry and per-platform syscalls.

components.name: Tests
components.responsibility: Host unit tests against a mock syscall layer, the gcov branch gate and the end-to-end smoke test, which also runs the invoker as `zazz` and as a script's shim.

components.name: Benchmarks
components.responsibility: Spawn-latency measurements of zazzle against a startup floor, a libc hello, grep and cat, and cold and warm refs timings.

components.name: zazzled
components.responsibility: The daemon the invoker talks to, for zazzle commands and (as zazz or a shim) zazz commands, and the binary it execs for `run` and `proxy`.

relationships.description: Sends every daemon command over its socket (prefixed `zazz` or `zazz exec-name NAME` when run under another name) and starts it when nothing listens; execs `zazzled wrap` and `zazzled proxy`.
Execs the free-disk-space binary beside itself.
Execs the fix-network binary beside itself.
unit.c includes zazzle_core.h with the mock; smoke.sh runs build/zazzle.
exit0.c reuses entry.h; run.sh and refs.sh time build/zazzle.
run.sh and refs.sh start the release zazzled on a temporary socket; refs.sh also times `zazzled run refs` cold.
